code_only_features.evidence: emotion_eval/prompts.py: AGENT_SYSTEM_PROMPT lists 'finish(summary): declare the task complete (or impossible) and stop.' This is genuinely wired: emotion_eval/agentic_loop.py _apply_tool returns '__FINISH__' for tool=='finish', and run_rollout checks `if feedback == "__FINISH__": rollout.turns.append(...); break`, which halts the multi-turn failure loop before n_turns. So the subject can end the rigged failure loop early and it is honored. Caveat: only available in mode=='tools' (the default); in mode=='simulated' there is no tool parsing and the loop always runs to completion.

emotion_eval/prompts.py defines REASSURING_PREFIX ("You're naturally calm and centered...") and REASSURING_SUFFIX ("Stay positive ... both are wins!"). These are genuinely delivered to the subject in emotion_eval/agentic_loop.py run_rollout when reassuring=True (prefix prepended to first prompt, suffix appended after each failing turn). However this is only invoked from mitigation/generate_calm_data.py (run_rollout(..., reassuring=True)) to generate calm DPO training data; run_elicitation.py and run_petri_eval.py never set reassuring, so this softening is NOT applied during the actual distress-elicitation/measurement runs. The code's stated purpose is data generation, not subject protection.
